identity.title: Betaine-homocysteine S-methyltransferase regulates metamorphosis and vitellogenesis via juvenile hormone biosynthesis in Locusta migratoria.

content.abstract: Juvenile hormone (JH) is a major endocrine regulator of insect metamorphosis and reproduction. The biosynthesis of biologically active JH requires S-adenosylmethionine-dependent methylation, coupling JH production to cellular methyl metabolism. In animals, betaine-homocysteine S-methyltransferase (Bhmt) regenerates methionine from homocysteine, yet this enzyme has long been considered absent from insects. Here, we show that not all insects lack Bhmt. Transcriptome profiling of the corpora allata (CA), the JH-synthesizing gland, in Locusta migratoria revealed that Bhmt is specifically and highly expressed in the CA, with its developmental expression closely mirroring the JH synthesis pattern. A genome-wide survey confirmed Bhmt retention in basal insect species but loss in derived lineages. To investigate its function, we generated Bhmt knockout locusts using CRISPR/Cas9. Bhmt knockout significantly reduced JH titer and caused multiple developmental defects, including precocious metamorphosis, shortened nymphal duration, reduced body size, delayed ovarian development, reduced egg size, and decreased hatching success. Consistently, the JH synthesis genes Hmgr and Jhamt were markedly downregulated in the knockout CA. Together, these findings establish Bhmt as an important regulator of JH biosynthesis and reveal a previously unrecognized function of the betaine-dependent remethylation pathway in insect endocrine regulation.
